Article Text:
The final balance stood at Rs 8,452 crore on March 31.

NEW DELHI: The PM CARES Fund, established to deal with emergency situations like Covid pandemic in 2020, recorded total receipts of Rs 8,452.95 crore in the financial year 2024-25, up from Rs 7,188.63 crore in the previous financial year, according to its audit report. The final balance stood at Rs 8,452 crore on March 31.Fixed deposits accounted for nearly 93 per cent of the fund's closing balance, with Rs 7,846.65 crore held in such deposits.Interest earned from these fixed deposits stood at Rs 469.38 crore during the year, making it the fund's largest source of income.Domestic donations to the fund declined to Rs 479.05 crore in FY25 from Rs 681.81 crore in FY24. Foreign donations also fell to Rs 9.28 lakh from Rs 11.35 lakh during the period.The fund's total payments during FY25 stood at Rs 87.85 lakh, compared with Rs 15.60 crore in the previous financial year.The figures show that while total receipts increased during FY25, donations from both domestic and foreign sources declined, while interest from fixed deposits accounted for the largest share of the fund's income.

Article Title: Use of EVs going up steadily: Consumption at public chargers rises by 72%
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Electricity consumption at public charging stations (PCS) jumped by over 72% in 2025-26, indicating a steady rise in the use of electric vehicles - private and commercial - as India's automotive sector shifts towards cleaner energy.Data compiled by the Central Electricity Authority (CEA) showed that 848 million units (MU) of electricity were consumed by public chargers in FY25, which increased to 1,460 MU in FY26. Over 74% of the electricity was consumed at heavy-duty public chargers used by electric buses, trucks, high-capacity passenger coaches and commercial fleet vehicles, while light and medium personal and commercial e-vehicles consumed 26%. In FY25, heavy-duty and medium and light vehicles accounted for 70% and 30% of electricity consumption, respectively.The data, however, is not comprehensive as it does not include electricity consumed by public chargers in all north-eastern states, as well as Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and the UTs of Puducherry, Chandigarh and Dadra and Nagar Haveli. CEA said power distribution companies in those states and UTs did not provide the relevant information.CEA said information on PCS was required to assess progress in the development of a reliable EV charging ecosystem, ensure energy security and reduce emission intensity, to make necessary policy interventions."The data on energy consumption in these EV charging stations is also important for the purpose of load forecasting, distribution system planning and integrated resource planning in the country," the report stated.Public chargers in Maharashtra consumed nearly 378 MU, or 26% of India's total energy consumption at PCS, followed by Delhi (359 MU), Karnataka (213 MU) and Telangana (111 MU).With govt pushing for adoption of EVs to foster a cleaner environment and achieve its net-zero emissions goal by 2070, total EV sales in India crossed 2.5 million units in 2025, marking a robust 24.6% year-on-year growth and accounting for nearly 8.5% of all new vehicle registrations, driven by strong growth in the two-wheeler, three-wheeler and passenger vehicle segments.
Article Summary: Electricity consumption at public charging stations (pcs) jumped by over 72% in 2025-26. Heavy-duty public chargers used by electric buses, trucks, high-capacity passenger coaches. Light and medium personal and commercial e-vehicles consumed 26%.

Article Title: Govt announces scheme to incentivise gas companies to expand PNG network
Article Text:
The government has approved the scheme to accelerate the expansion of domestic piped natural gas (PNG) connections, with the aim of making clean, safe and affordable cooking fuel accessible to more households across the country.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: To promote the expansion of PNG network and ensure more families start using piped gas in their kitchens, the government on Tuesday approved an incentive scheme promising additional lower-priced domestic gas to distribution companies for each new connection activated by them.According to the government, city gas distribution (CGD) companies have made provision for more than 1.7 crore domestic PNG connections across the country, but the actual number of billed or active connections is only over 1.1 crore. Under the new scheme, CGD companies will be allocated an additional 200 standard cubic metres of domestically produced, lower-priced (APM) gas for each unbilled connection converted into a working one above the threshold level.The additional gas allocation will substitute the costlier liquefied natural gas that CGD entities currently procure for their compressed natural gas (transport) segment, thereby lowering their overall gas-sourcing costs.“The resulting cost savings are expected to shorten the payback period for capital expenditure incurred on domestic PNG connections from around 10 years to approximately 3 years -- giving CGD entities a strong financial incentive to expand household PNG connectivity more rapidly and bringing the benefits of clean, safe and affordable piped cooking gas to a larger number of Indian households in the months ahead,” the petroleum ministry said in a statement.
Article Summary: The government has approved the scheme to accelerate the expansion of domestic piped natural gas (png) connections. The aim is to make clean, safe and affordable cooking fuel accessible to more households across the country. Under the new scheme, cgd companies will be allocated an additional 200 standard cubic metres of domestically produced, lower-priced (apm) gas.

Article Title: 'No safe harbour if law violated; message has gone home': Government sources on talks with Meta
Article Text:
Discussions with Meta have focused heavily on the company's handling of CSAM and other harmful online content (representative image)

Govt seeks stronger local sensitivity in content moderation

WhatsApp usernames, platform regulation also under scrutiny

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The government has made it clear to Meta that safe-harbour protection will not be available if the company violates Indian law, with sources saying the message has been conveyed during recent discussions between the two sides over content moderation and child sexual abuse material (CSAM).“Seen some action on CSAM issue; govt clear no safe harbour if law violated; message has gone home,” government sources said, according to news agency PTI.The discussions with Meta have focused heavily on the company's handling of CSAM and other harmful online content, as well as its compliance with India's legal framework.According to sources cited by news agency ANI, Meta has become more cautious about CSAM-related content and is taking steps to filter out unlawful material.The government has also conveyed that it has acted strictly within the powers available under the existing legal and statutory framework.The government has maintained that its objective is not to censor social media platforms or suppress legitimate speech, but to ensure that platforms operating in India comply with Indian laws and do not create circumstances that could adversely affect the country's social fabric.The discussions have also focused on Meta's content moderation systems, with the government stressing the need for greater sensitivity to India's linguistic and cultural diversity.Government sources said moderation teams cannot rely solely on global standards and need a better understanding of Indian languages and cultural contexts when making decisions about content.The government has also raised concerns over deepfakes and other forms of synthetically generated content. Sources said AI-generated material should be clearly labelled so users can distinguish between synthetic and authentic content.This, the government said, is a matter of the “user's right to know” whether the content they are viewing is genuine or AI-generated.Earlier discussions had also examined Meta's recommendation and virality systems, including concerns over why flagged synthetic content could continue to resurface or be amplified. The government had sought details of the company's safeguards and content moderation mechanisms, while stressing that material identified as unlawful or harmful should not continue to be recommended.The government is separately examining the issue of WhatsApp usernames from an industry-wide perspective, rather than treating it as an issue specific to Meta.Sources said the Centre would continue to monitor the matter across messaging platforms.The broader discussions have covered Meta's compliance with Indian law, its content policies, moderation systems and safeguards.The government has previously questioned the company's eligibility for safe-harbour protection under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act, which provides intermediaries protection from liability for third-party content subject to specified conditions.Government sources said similar debates over platform regulation have emerged in Western liberal democracies as well, underlining that the challenge is not unique to India.At the same time, officials stressed that cultural and social contexts differ between countries and that reasonable restrictions on freedom of speech remain constitutionally applicable in India.The latest discussions follow several rounds of engagement between Meta's global team and the ministry of electronics and information technology over CSAM, deepfakes, bots, synthetic content, recommendation algorithms and compliance with Indian laws.The government has maintained that it is not seeking a wholesale overhaul of Meta's algorithms, but wants the company's platforms and moderation mechanisms to operate in accordance with Indian law and account adequately for the country's linguistic and cultural context.
Article Summary: The government has made it clear to meta that safe-harbour protection will not be available if the company violates indian law. Discussions with meta have focused heavily on the company's handling of csam and other harmful online content. The government has also raised concerns over deepfakes and other forms of synthetically generated content.

Article Title: CEA bats for E10 fuel; not feasibile, say officials
Article Text:
Officials were taken aback by the Chief Economic Adviser's comments regarding the availability of E10 fuel

NEW DELHI: An opinion piece by chief economic adviser (CEA) V Anantha Nageswaran on ethanol blending has rekindled the debate whether govt should look at making E10 (10% ethanol blended petrol) available for older vehicles manufactured before April 2023.Officials, dealing with the issue and countering the narrative against E20 fuel for the past few weeks, admitted that the CEA’s views came as a surprise for them as it bats for making E10 available as an option at fuel stations. This is likely to push the demand for making lower-blend of fuel available in addition to E20, they said, adding it won’t be easy logistically and considering that an ecosystem has been in place for 20% of blending that’s linked to the rural economy.TOI has learnt that as of now, there is no discussion within govt to provide the option of E10 at fuel stations. While there has been a campaign demanding petrol with lower ethanol content, a govt official said there was no discussion so far on reverting to fuel with 10% blending. The official said creating additional infrastructure to dispense E10 petrol is not only logistically difficult, but may also lead to practical issues such as pricing and distribution. “Also, allowing the sale of E10 would mean govt is accepting E20 petrol is not good for older vehicles which is not the case. Studies have shown E20 does not cause any mechanical issues,” said another official.
Article Summary: Officials were taken aback by the chief economic adviser's comments regarding the availability of e10 fuel. As of now, there is no discussion within govt to provide the option of e 10 at fuel stations. While there has been a campaign demanding petrol with lower ethanol content, a govt official said there was no discussion so far on reverting to fuel with 10%.

Article Title: “We want your pee, please give us your pee": Why Jason Kelce singing about urine in a meadow is actually the smartest marketing campaign of 2026
Article Text:
Jason Kelce "we want you pee" ad (Getty Images)

What exactly is Jason Kelce asking fans to do in the Garage Beer and Liquid Death campaign?

Why is Jason Kelce the face of Garage Beer and how big is the brand now?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jason Kelce has made some memorable moments since retiring from the NFL, but nothing quite prepared the internet for this one. On Tuesday, August 18, the former Philadelphia Eagles center and Garage Beer co-owner appeared in a new joint campaign with Liquid Death, asking fans to do something most brands would never dare request: send in their urine. Not as a prank. Not as a stunt with no point. Kelce and the brands are dead serious about the cause -- AI data centers across the United States are consuming up to 5 million gallons of water per day to cool their servers, and they want you to help fix it. With your pee.The ad opens with Jason Kelce sitting on a toilet, filling up a jar, and explaining the problem directly to the camera: *"AI data centers waste millions of gallons of water. That's why Liquid Death and Garage Beer decided to team up: We want your pee … to cool these data centers."*It only gets stranger from there. Kelce steps outside into an open meadow, joins Liquid Death's mascot Murder Man, and breaks into song. The chorus, which has already lodged itself into the brains of anyone who has seen the ad, goes: "We want your pee, please give us your pee. Let's pee on computers together. 'Cause we need lots of pee, endless gallons of pee.Join our important endeavor. We want your pee, please give us your pee. Let's pee on computers together to save humanity, we want your pee."The campaign, titled "We Want Your Pee," is framed as a P[EE].S.A. -- a public service announcement with a very specific twist. It is built around a real statistic: there are more than 4,000 data centers operating in the United States, and each one can consume up to 5 million gallons of water daily. Human urine, according to the Cleveland Clinic, is between 91 and 96 percent water. Humans produce anywhere from three to eight cups per day. The math, at least in concept, is right there.The campaign will run with paid support across Garage Beer and Liquid Death's social channels and on connected TV, with a limited "Coolant Collector" product also being sold as part of the launch.Kelce, 38, and his brother Travis Kelce became co-owners of Garage Beer in June 2024, purchasing a majority stake and taking the largest investor positions in the company. This was not a passive celebrity endorsement deal. Garage Beer CEO Andy Sauer told the Wall Street Journal that the Kelce brothers are genuinely hands-on in how the brand operates."It's pretty emblematic on how they both operate," Sauer said. "It's an always-on relationship. It's two people with the same vision and belief in beer, jumping into it."The brand itself is an American-style light craft lager at 95 calories, launched in 2023. By September 2025, it had been valued at $200 million. When Jason signed on, he was clear about why it appealed to him: "People crave quality and simplicity, and Garage Beer nails both for me. We are light beer drinkers and Garage is the best light beer. For me, the brand fits my lifestyle, and having a few beers is a great excuse to get the neighbors together.Travis echoed that energy: "I think everyone knows I like to have a couple beers now and then, so being an owner of Garage Beer and heavily involved in making the best light beer is exciting, man! There is nothing better to bring people together than an ice-cold beer, and for Jason and me that is what beer is all about -- friends, family and fun."Outside Garage Beer, Jason owns Underdog Apparel and has collaborated with Homage on merchandise tied to the "New Heights" podcast he runs with Travis. He has done ad work for Buffalo Wild Wings, Campbell's, and Bazooka Candy Brands over the years. But this one is different. This campaign is not about moving product through a 30-second spot. It is about tapping into a real public tension around AI, water usage, and Big Tech — and doing it in the most Jason Kelce way possible: loud, weird, and oddly earnest.
Article Summary: Jason kelce, co-owner of garage beer, stars in new ad for liquid death. The ad asks fans to send in their urine to cool down ai data centers. Data centers consume up to 5 million gallons of water per day to cool their servers. This campaign is not about moving product through a 30-second spot.

Article Title: Accenture CEO Julie Sweet makes a 'vacation request' to employees for this August
Article Text:
Julie Sweet asks employees to help deliver a strong fourth quarter

Why Accenture changed its vacation policy

AI remains a key concern for Accenture investors

Accenture CEO Julie Sweet is asking employees to think twice before taking time off this August as the company pushes for a strong finish to its financial year. In a rare one-time policy change, Accenture will allow staff to carry forward any unused vacation days into the next fiscal year instead of requiring them to use the leave before August ends. The move comes alongside Julie Sweet's call for employees to focus on winning new business and generating more revenue in the final weeks of the quarter after the consulting giant reported weaker-than-expected quarterly results. Accenture’s new policy will give its workers more flexibility while helping keep more employees available during the company's year-end sales push.In a memo seen by Bloomberg, Accenture CEO Sweet urged employees to contribute to improving fourth-quarter results by finding new ways to serve clients and generate revenue. "Our shareholders are counting on us to deliver a strong quarter in Q4 — everyone can contribute," Sweet wrote.“This means we all need to find more ways to serve clients that create more revenue in the quarter and to originate more sales (small, large, mega) to finish strong,” she added.According to Bloomberg, the company has also allowed employees to carry over unused vacation days into the next financial year, which begins on September 1.Normally, staff must use their vacation before the fiscal year ends.People familiar with the matter told the publication that the temporary policy change is part of the company's effort to keep more employees working during August rather than taking leave before their vacation days expire. Another person familiar with the matter said the one-time change is also meant to give employees greater flexibility.The move comes after weaker-than-expected results. Accenture reported a 2% decline in new bookings for the quarter ended May 31 and projected fourth-quarter revenue of $17.75 billion to $18.4 billion, below analysts' average estimate of $18.47 billion. Following the earnings announcement in June, Accenture shares fell about 20% in one day, one of the company's biggest single-day declines on record.The earnings report also intensified concerns that artificial intelligence could disrupt the consulting industry in the near term, even though Julie Sweet has described AI as a "tailwind" for Accenture's business.Bloomberg Intelligence said in a recent research note: “AI remains the dominant concern for services and consulting. Though management positions Accenture as a long-term AI beneficiary, tangible evidence that AI is accelerating demand is limited.”
Article Summary: Julie sweet asks employees to help deliver a strong fourth quarter for accenture. In a rare one-time policy change, accenture will allow staff to carry forward any unused vacation days into the next fiscal year. The move comes alongside sweet's call for employees to focus on winning new business and generating more revenue.

Article Title: Who is Gautam Rangarajan? Indian-origin strategist appointed to key role by UK PM Andy Burnham
Article Text:
Indian-origin strategist Gautam Rangarajan.

Who is Gautam Rangarajan ?

What will Gautam Rangarajan do at No. 10?

Burnham's government overhaul

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has appointed Indian-origin strategist and former BBC executive Gautam Rangarajan as an Expert Adviser on Structure and Process in a newly created role at 10 Downing Street.Rangarajan, who brings decades of experience in strategy, organisational transformation and media, is set to take up the position this week.Rangarajan is a senior strategist and media executive with more than two decades of experience across media, creative industries and public service broadcasting.Before his new government role, he spent more than 30 years at the BBC, beginning his career as a radio music producer and eventually rising to become the broadcaster's Group Director for Strategy and Performance.His experience includes developing strategy in rapidly changing markets, leading large-scale transformation initiatives and handling complex policy and financial negotiations.The exact details of Rangarajan's responsibilities are yet to be outlined. However, the UK PM's office said his appointment draws on his experience in corporate strategy and transformation.His role comes as Burnham undertakes a broader restructuring of the machinery of government, including the creation of the Office for the Prime Minister and Cabinet.Rangarajan is expected to play a role in the planned transformation at the heart of the British government.Away from strategy and public service, Rangarajan also has a creative side. He describes himself as a professional choral singer and music producer, alongside his work in corporate strategy and organisational transformation.The appointment comes as Burnham reshapes his government following his recent rise to the role of Labour Party leader and Prime Minister.His administration has announced structural changes, including the launch of No. 10 North in Manchester and the creation of the Office for the Prime Minister and Cabinet.While the full scope of Rangarajan's new role remains unclear, his appointment places the former BBC executive at the centre of the UK government's planned transformation.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox: "I think the scariest person in the world is the person with…" - a lesson on humour, perspective and facing hard times with lightness
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox (AP photo)

Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox

"I think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor"

Where this quote actually comes from

Why humour matters most during genuinely difficult stretches

How humour actually helps people manage stress

Why laughing at your own mistakes actually matters

Why humour can genuinely strengthen relationships

Michael J. Fox's own perspective on adversity

Why humour is not the same thing as avoiding a real problem

Why being naturally serious is not actually a flaw

Other memorable quotes by Michael J. Fox

"One's dignity may be assaulted, vandalized and cruelly mocked, but it can never be taken away unless it is surrendered."

"I am careful not to confuse excellence with perfection."

"Family is not an important thing. It's everything."

"Acceptance doesn't mean resignation; it means understanding that something is what it is and that there's got to be a way through it."

Why people still find meaning in this quote

Humour can genuinely change how a difficult moment actually feels. A stressful situation seems lighter once someone finds a reason to laugh, and a serious problem often becomes easier to approach once it can be seen from another angle. It can create a little distance from fear, frustration and uncertainty, even when the circumstances themselves have not changed. Michael J. Fox , the actor and Parkinson's disease advocate, put a striking twist on that idea. "I think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor," he said. Not being able to laugh, in his framing, is not simply a personality quirk. It genuinely limits how someone can respond to life, and coming from someone who has lived with a serious, lifelong illness for decades, the line carries a good deal more weight than a passing joke.This line comes from an interview Fox gave to journalist Amy Wallace, published on Reader's Digest's website. Fox is not really suggesting that a humourless person is dangerous in any literal sense. He is pointing at the seriousness that tends to surround someone who cannot laugh at themselves, cannot recognise irony, and cannot find any lightness in a genuinely difficult moment. Humour creates real distance from a problem.It lets someone acknowledge that something is hard without letting it completely take over.Life inevitably brings disappointment, uncertainty and real stress. Humour cannot solve every problem on its own, but it can genuinely change how someone responds to one. Being able to laugh during a hard period offers a small emotional break, and it can help people communicate when a direct, serious conversation feels too uncomfortable to actually have. None of this means every situation deserves to be treated as a joke. Humour and genuine seriousness can exist side by side.Stress tends to narrow someone's attention down entirely onto the immediate problem in front of them. A moment of real laughter can interrupt that cycle. Research into humour and stress has suggested that positive humour can genuinely influence mood and help people cope with stressful experiences, and laughter itself is linked to physiological changes, including a release of muscle tension. None of this should be overstated. Humour is never a substitute for professional help or a practical solution when someone faces a genuinely serious problem. As an everyday coping tool, though, it can offer a genuinely useful shift in perspective.One of the most valuable forms of humour is simply being able to laugh at your own missteps. Nobody gets everything right. People mispronounce words, misjudge situations and occasionally embarrass themselves, and someone who can acknowledge a mistake without being consumed by embarrassment tends to find it easier to actually learn from it. Self-directed humour also tends to make social interactions considerably more comfortable, since it signals that a person does not expect flawless perfection from either themselves or anyone else around them.Shared laughter helps people form real connections. Friends, colleagues and family members often use humour to build a sense of familiarity and trust, and a well-placed joke can break tension that a serious conversation might struggle to shift on its own. There is an important line here worth being clear about, between humour that actually brings people together and humour that humiliates someone else. Jokes built on cruelty or prejudice tend to damage relationships rather than genuinely strengthen them, and the most constructive kind of humour has never really needed anyone else to get hurt.Fox became one of the most recognisable actors of his generation through films and television, including Back to the Future and Family Ties. In 1991, at the age of 29, he was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. He later made the diagnosis public and became a prominent advocate for Parkinson's research through the Michael J. Fox Foundation. His public approach to living with the condition has consistently included honesty, genuine optimism and humour, which gives his comments about laughter an extra dimension. His point was never that difficult experiences are inherently funny. It is that holding onto a sense of humour can help someone preserve real perspective while actually facing a genuine challenge. His decades-long relationship with humour, cultivated alongside a chronic illness he never chose, reveals that laughter was never a denial of hardship for Fox, but a deliberate, hard-won tool for maintaining perspective and genuine hope through real adversity.There is a meaningful difference between using humour to cope with something difficult and using it to avoid actually dealing with it at all. Some problems genuinely require serious attention and real action, and nobody can simply laugh away financial difficulty, illness or grief. What humour can offer instead is a small amount of emotional breathing space while someone continues addressing the actual underlying issue, which is really the whole distinction worth holding onto here.Fox's quote is deliberately provocative, and it should not be read as suggesting that serious people are inherently unpleasant. Some people naturally have quieter personalities, or simply express humour in a different way. The broader lesson is really about flexibility rather than personality type. Someone who can be genuinely serious when it matters, while still finding moments of humour elsewhere, tends to have more ways of responding to life's challenges than someone who treats every single situation with exactly the same level of weight.Humour is easy to underrate, since it can look insignificant next to more obviously serious qualities like intelligence or discipline. Even so, the ability to laugh genuinely shapes how people communicate, handle their own mistakes and respond to real difficulty. Fox's quote offers a deliberately provocative reminder that life does not always need to be approached with complete seriousness. There will be moments when humour is genuinely inappropriate, and problems that cannot be laughed away at all. In between those moments, though, holding onto a sense of humour tends to keep people connected, flexible and hopeful, which is really the whole point behind the line.
Article Summary: "i think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor" michael j. Fox, actor and parkinson's disease advocate. Not being able to laugh is not simply a personality quirk. It genuinely limits how someone can respond to life. Michael j. Fox was one of the most recognisable actors of his generation.

Article Title: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu says rising memory and AI token prices are making business very difficult: ‘We have …’
Article Text:
Sridhar Vembu: Memory prices have made business ‘very difficult’

Sridhar Vembu says the era of ‘free’ memory is over

Zoho co-founder Sridhar Vembu has raised concerns over the sharp rise in computer memory prices, saying the increase, along with the cost of AI tokens, is making it harder to run businesses. Sridhar Vembu was responding to a Tom’s Hardware report that said memory prices have jumped as much as 500% in the past 12 months, with some DDR5 RAM kits now costing nearly 10 times their lowest recorded prices. The Zoho founder said companies have so far tried to avoid passing these higher costs to customers, but added that holding prices steady is becoming increasingly difficult.Reacting to the report in a post on X, Sridhar Vembu wrote: “Memory prices, along with AI token prices have made business very difficult. We have held back from raising prices but it is becoming hard.”His comments come as memory prices have climbed sharply over the past year. According to historical pricing data cited by Tom's Hardware, a 64GB DDR5-5600 kit that averaged around $191 in August 2025 was priced at about $1,118 in August 2026, an increase of about 485%.Higher-capacity memory has seen an even bigger jump from its previous lows. A 128GB DDR5-6400 kit was recently listed at $3,399, compared with a lowest tracked price of $329.The increase is not limited to DDR5. DDR4 prices have also risen, with the report showing year-on-year increases ranging from about 120% to 177% across the memory kits it tracked.In the post, Sridhar Vembu also used the sharp price increase to make a broader point about how software is developed. He argued that programming languages and software tools will have to become more efficient as memory becomes more expensive.“A techncial note: for a long time, programming languages were designed with the assumption that memory is ‘free’. That era has now ended. We need highly memory efficient languages and smarter compilers, even for AI to use,” Vembu wrote.He added: “Safety of code and productivity in writing code cannot come at the expense of memory bloat. That is my area of research.”
Article Summary: Sridhar vembu: memory prices have made business ‘very difficult’ he was responding to a tom’s hardware report that said memory prices have jumped as much as 500% in the past 12 months. The zoho founder said companies have so far tried to avoid passing these higher costs to customers.

Article Title: Apple left a video of its camera AirPods inside a Mac update, and this is what they look like
Article Text:
Apple demoed a camera you can't see, in a video it didn't mean to publish.

AirPods cameras are for Siri, not for you to click photos

A frame from the demo video Apple left in macOS 26.7, alongside a closer look at the bud. The stem is thicker than the AirPods Pro 3. (Image: MacRumors/Aaron Perris)

Apple employees have been wearing prototypes for months

A September launch could be on the table, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro

The first real look at Apple's camera AirPods didn't come from the usual suspects. It came from Apple, by mistake. Buried in the macOS Tahoe 26.7 release candidate that landed Monday is a short demo video showing a man wearing AirPods holding up a book, with a Siri voiceover explaining that Visual Intelligence makes "your world becomes savable" and that you can ask it to save what you're looking at for later. MacRumors found the clip.You have to look twice to spot what's different. The bud in the video could pass for an AirPods Pro 3. No visible lens, no sensor housing, just a stem that reads slightly thicker than the current one. MacRumors also found the release candidate littered with references to codename B790, including an error string about an image stream failing on the left bud. Elsewhere in the same build: a warning telling users to keep the AirPods uncovered so the system can read their surroundings accurately. Long hair, evidently, is a known problem.What the cameras actually do is narrower than it sounds. According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, they capture low-resolution visual information for Siri to reason about, not photos or video. Look at what's in your fridge, ask what to cook. Walk somewhere and get directions that account for what's in front of you.The demo fits that description. Nobody takes a picture in it. A man looks at a book, Siri saves the book, and that is the whole feature.Gurman has also described longer stems and an LED that lights up when visual data goes to the cloud. Neither turns up in the video.Apple testers have been using prototypes daily since at least May, Bloomberg reported at the time, at the design validation test stage. That is the step immediately before production validation, which means the physical design is locked and what follows is a manufacturing problem rather than a product one. Everything after DVT is about yields and tooling. It also explains why the software looks finished. A team that far along has hardware stable enough to build onboarding screens against, which is exactly what turned up in macOS this week.Earlier this month, Bloomberg reported that camera AirPods could arrive as soon as this year, pulling forward a device most people had penciled in for 2027. Apple's iPhone event is expected in early September, where the iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max and the first foldable iPhone are due.One wrinkle worth keeping straight: B790 is not the camera AirPods Gurman has been writing about since 2025. That model, B798, slipped to 2027 after Apple's Siri delays. B790 is a separate project that got there first.Apple, as usual, hasn't confirmed any of it. But a release candidate is the last build before public release, and this one already has setup screens and error messages for the thing. That normally means the hardware is done. September will tell us the rest.
Article Summary: Airpods cameras are for siri, not for you to click photos. The bud in the video could pass for an airpods pro 3. Apple employees have been wearing prototypes for months. A september launch could be on the table, alongside the iphone 18 pro.

Article Title: Biggest US grid operator has a ‘shutdown proposal’ that shows tension between data centers and power grids in America
Article Text:
Representative image

Why grid operators are worried with rapid expansion of datacenters

PJM Interconnection, the largest electrical grid operator in the US, has proposed a framework that would require data centers to switch to backup generators when regional power reserves hit dangerously low levels. According to a report in Reuters, the proposal aligns with President Donald Trump's "Ratepayer Protection Pledge," a non-binding initiative aimed at shielding residential consumers from escalating costs tied to surging data center power demands, according to PJM.Under the proposed emergency procedure, utilities would be instructed to curtail or transfer electricity demand from data centers and other heavy energy consumers before imposing blackouts on residential households. This means that PJM Interconnection is proposing a shutdown of data centers in emergencies. In the event that the power grid is in danger of shutting down, they want data centers to be shut down first.However, PJM noted that it currently lacks direct authority to mandate such curtailments and must rely on cooperation from individual state regulators.PJM manages electricity distribution for 67 million people across a 13-state region stretching from Washington, D.C.to Chicago. The move underscores intensifying friction between the rapid expansion of energy-hungry data infrastructure and the capacity of the aging U.S. power grid.The grid operator's recent capacity auction saw prices hit a regulatory cap of $325 per megawatt-day. Despite those price signals designed to spur new power generation, PJM still faced a roughly 6.8-gigawatt shortfall against its projected reliability requirements, heightening the risk of system-wide blackouts.To better manage system loads, PJM is also seeking to establish a registry to monitor the locations and power consumption of data centers and other massive electricity users. The rapid proliferation of data facilities has evolved into a contentious political issue across PJM's footprint, notably in Northern Virginia, which hosts the world's largest concentration of data hubs. Local communities increasingly voice concerns over noise, neighborhood disruption, and the risk of absorbing the utility bills required to power the tech sector's expansion.
Article Summary: Pjm interconnection, the largest electrical grid operator in the us, has proposed a framework that would require data centers to switch to backup generators. The move underscores intensifying friction between the rapid expansion of energy-hungry data infrastructure and the capacity of the aging u.s. power grid.

Article Title: Why Google is making headlines in Berkshire's biggest quarter of stock-buying following Warren Buffett's exit as CEO
Article Text:
Warren Buffett ’s legacy and Abel’s role

Other portfolio changes

Cash deployment

Berkshire Hathway has sharply increased its stake in Alphabet during its biggest quarter of stock buying in years. According to a report by Business Insider, under CEO Greg Abel, Berkshire boosted its holdings by 83% to about 106 million shares worth $38 billion at the end of June in Alphabet. The conglomerate agreed to purchase $10 billion worth of Alphabet stock at a discount in a private placement in June, and added another 19.6 million shares on the open market last quarter. Alphabet is now Berkshire’s third‑largest US holding, behind Apple ($66 billion) and American Express ($51 billion).The size of the Alphabet bet stands out given Buffett's long-standing reluctance to invest heavily in technology stocks throughout most of his career, with Apple as the notable exception. He has historically preferred businesses like Coca-Cola and Geico over tech names. Even so, Buffett has said he personally made the call to invest in Alphabet last year, and with Abel now serving as CEO while Buffett remains chairman, the position appears to reflect shared decision-making between the two rather than a clean break from Buffett's past preferences.Alphabet's stock has climbed roughly 170% over the past three years, with investors continuing to bet that the search-and-advertising giant will emerge as one of the biggest beneficiaries of the ongoing AI boom.Alphabet wasn't the only shift in Berkshire's holdings last quarter. The firm boosted its stake in Delta Air Lines by 44%, bringing that position to $5.4 billion as of June 30. It also established a new stake in D.R. Horton and added significantly to its existing positions in Lennar and Macy's.On the other side of the ledger, Berkshire roughly halved its stakes in Capital One and Nucor, trimmed its holdings in Bank of America and Kroger, and exited a smaller position in Constellation Brands entirely.The second‑quarter update showed Berkshire spent $23.5 billion on stocks while selling only $3.7 billion, ending 14 straight quarters as a net seller. It also executed $4.5 billion in buybacks, reducing its cash pile from $380 billion to $365 billion.

Article Title: In 2005 for the first time, scientists documented giant squid in their natural habitat, since then many mysteries about their lives remain in ...
Article Text:
A diorama unlike any other in the museum

The real-life battle behind the display

Decades of mystery, only recently interrupted

An unassuming black box near the American Museum of Natural History's iconic blue whale draws in unsuspecting visitors to one of the museum's most striking exhibits, according to a Popular Science report. Every few seconds, a light flashes inside an otherwise pitch-black display, briefly revealing a row of sharp teeth and reddish tentacles as a sperm whale clamps down on a giant squid. The Sperm Whale and Giant Squid Diorama offers a rare, dramatic glimpse into one of the ocean's most mysterious predator-prey relationships, one that scientists are still working to fully understand.Unlike most of AMNH's other displays, this diorama has no glass front. Instead, its dark, reflective interior creates a mirror-like effect that reportedly confused early visitors into thinking the exhibit was empty. The darkness isn't incidental, it's designed to recreate the lightless conditions of the deep ocean, where sunlight never reaches.That same design also makes the diorama unusually labor-intensive to clean. In a video recently shared on social media, AMNH Exhibition Maintenance staffer Janet Spiller can be seen using a backpack vacuum fitted with fiber pole attachments to reach into the exhibit's nooks and crannies, a job that can take a single person up to four hours to complete.The scene depicted in the diorama reflects a genuine and extreme biological encounter. Sperm whales (Physeter macrocephalus) are known to dive more than 6,500 feet, a depth equivalent to stacking roughly four and a half Empire State Buildings on top of one another, and can remain submerged for over 60 minutes at a time in pursuit of giant squid (Architeuthis dux).Much of what scientists know about this underwater clash comes from indirect evidence rather than direct observation. Sperm whales are sometimes found with circular marks on their skin, believed to be sucker marks left behind from squid fighting to escape. Researchers have also recovered giant squid beaks, the hard biting structures used by the animal, inside the stomachs of sperm whales, offering further proof of these deep-sea encounters.Despite the drama depicted in exhibits like this one, giant squid remain one of the ocean's most elusive animals. Scientists did not document a giant squid in its natural habitat on camera until 2005, and even now, many aspects of the species' life in the deep ocean remain largely unknown. The persistence of that mystery is part of what continues to make the predator-prey relationship between sperm whales and giant squid such a compelling subject for both researchers and museum visitors alike.
Article Summary: The sperm whale and giant squid diorama offers a rare, dramatic glimpse into one of the ocean's most mysterious predator-prey relationships.
